les: Waar op die wêreld is dit warm, en waar is dit koud?
kaps_punt: Warm, gematigde en koue streke van die wêreld - insluitende Januarie en Julie temperatuurkaarte

items.bewering: Dit is nie oral op die aarde ewe warm nie.
items.bron: Ritter, The Physical Environment (Ohio University / LibreTexts), 'Air Temperature - global patterns': temperature changes with latitude, and the annual range is smallest in the tropics and largest in the interiors of subpolar continents.

items.bewering: Ons deel die wêreld in drie soorte streke volgens hoe warm dit gewoonlik is.
items.bron: AMS Glossary of Meteorology, 'hot belt', 'temperate belt', 'cold cap' and 'Köppen-Supan line' (glossary.ametsoc.org): Supan (1879) divided the earth into three thermal belts by temperature (hot belt where the annual mean is above 20°C; cold caps where the warmest month averages below 10°C; temperate belt in between). Wikipedia 'Geographical zone' and the 1810-1823 Encyclopaedia Britannica describe the same three zones as 'heat zones'. A division by usual temperature is therefore an established basis, and it is the one the rest of the lesson follows (Greenland in the cold region, for example).

items.bewering: In die meeste dele van die warm streek bly dit die hele jaar omtrent ewe warm.
items.bron: Ritter, The Physical Environment, 9.4.1 Tropical Rain Forest (LibreTexts): the annual temperature range rarely exceeds 3-4°F and is smaller than the daily range. 9.4.3 Tropical Wet/Dry (Savanna): a somewhat larger annual range, but monthly means stay between about 18°C and above 25°C. The qualifier 'die meeste dele' is needed and correct: hot deserts at the edges of the belt (the Sahara, for example) have clearly larger annual ranges, but most of the belt is ocean, rain forest and savanna.

items.bewering: Die gematigde streke het 'n warm tyd van die jaar en 'n koue tyd.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Temperate climate' and 'Geographical zone': temperate zones have four seasons, with a warmest season (summer) and a colder season (winter), and wider annual ranges than the tropics.

items.bewering: In die koue streke is dit die grootste deel van die jaar koud en die warmer tyd is kort.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters, 'Polar climate': 'short, cool summers and long, cold winters'. AMS Glossary 'cold cap': even the warmest month averages below 10°C.

items.bewering: Die ewenaar is 'n lyn om die middel van die aarde. Dit deel die aarde in twee gelyke helftes: die noordelike en die suidelike halfrond.
items.bron: Britannica Kids, 'hemisphere': an imaginary line called the equator divides the Northern and Southern hemispheres; the equator is 0° latitude. Encyclopaedia Britannica (cited by the Curtin University library): a great circle equidistant from both poles, so it halves the globe. Note only: the lesson does not say the line is imaginary. That is not false (it is a line on every map and globe), and is recorded here only so a person can decide whether 'denkbeeldige' is worth adding.

items.bewering: Die warm streek lê in 'n breë band om die ewenaar, en die noorde van Brasilië lê daarin.
items.bron: Library of Congress Country Studies, Brazil (countrystudies.us/brazil/23.htm): 'the equator traverses the mouth of the Amazon'; '90 percent of the country is within the tropical zone'; the Tropic of Capricorn crosses at about the latitude of São Paulo. True as stated. Note only: about nine-tenths of Brazil lies in the tropics, so a learner should not take 'die noorde' to mean that only the north is warm. The sentence does not say that.

items.bewering: Die koue streke lê heel in die noorde by Groenland en heel in die suide by Antarktika.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Geography of Greenland' (about 81% under an ice sheet, with tundra on the coast and ice cap inland, so nearly all of it is classed as polar). EBSCO 'Polar climate': polar climates cover the Arctic, Greenland and Antarctica. Southern Greenland lies south of the Arctic Circle, but by temperature (the basis the lesson itself states) it is still tundra, with summers between 0°C and 10°C.

items.bewering: Die gematigde streke lê tussen die warm band en die koue streke.
items.bron: AMS Glossary 'temperate belt' (between the hot belt and the cold caps). Wikipedia 'Geographical zone' (the temperate zones lie between the tropics and the polar circles).

items.bewering: Die grootste deel van Suid-Afrika lê in die gematigde streek van die suidelike halfrond.
items.bron: gov.za 'Geography & climate': South Africa stretches from 22°S to 35°S, and its subtropical location, ocean on three sides and interior altitude give 'warm temperate conditions'. The Tropic of Capricorn (about 23.4°S) crosses only Limpopo, so only a small northern strip lies north of it. 'Die grootste deel' is the correct form: 'heel Suid-Afrika' would be wrong under a latitude reading.

items.bewering: 'n Temperatuurkaart van die wêreld wys met kleure hoe warm dit oral is.
items.bron: Australian Space Agency, 'Colour by Numbers - Earth Observation' (space.gov.au): a temperature map with a colour for each temperature band. Colorado State University Climate Center, 'Make a Temperature Map' (climate.colostate.edu): a colour for each 5-degree band. Note only: some temperature maps show temperature with isotherm lines (Merriam-Webster; Wikipedia 'Contour line') rather than colours, or with both. Describing the usual coloured kind is incomplete, not false.

items.bewering: By die kaart staan 'n sleutel wat sê vir watter reeks temperature elke kleur staan.
items.bron: Australian Space Agency, 'Colour by Numbers' (a key of temperature bands, for example 23-25°C up to 38-40°C, one colour per range). Colorado State Climate Center temperature-map exercise (one colour per 5°F band). GISGeography 'map legend': the legend or key explains what each colour stands for.

items.bewering: Lees eers die sleutel en soek dan jou plek op die kaart. Hou daardie kleur teen die sleutel en lees af in watter reeks jou plek val.
items.bron: Follows from how a banded key works (same sources as above: each colour on the key is paired with one temperature range, so matching a place's colour to the key gives its range). The method is sound for the banded colour maps the lesson describes.

items.bewering: Dieselfde plek is nie die hele jaar ewe warm nie. Een kaart kan dus nie 'n plek se temperatuur vir die hele jaar wys nie.
items.bron: Ritter, 'Air Temperature - global patterns', and the Tropical Rain Forest section: every place has an annual range, even if it is as small as 2°C at equatorial stations such as Pontianak. Tested as a set with block 1 ('omtrent ewe warm' in the warm region) and block 5 (the warm band looks much the same on both maps): the three do not contradict each other, because 'not exactly equally warm' is true everywhere. Note only: the opening sentence is general and the qualification comes in the neighbouring blocks.

items.bewering: Daarom is daar een kaart vir Januarie en een vir Julie. Die twee kaarte saam wys hoeveel 'n plek tussen Januarie en Julie verander.
items.bron: University of Wisconsin meteorology notes and Ritter 'Air Temperature' (people.ohio.edu): January and July are the usual months for mapping the seasonal extremes, and the annual range is commonly taken as the difference between the July and January means. Environment Canada / Canadian National Atlas, 'Temperature - January and July' (open.canada.ca): a standard pair of mean-temperature maps.

items.bewering: Naby die ewenaar lyk die warm band op albei kaarte omtrent dieselfde.
items.bron: Ritter, Tropical Rain Forest (annual range rarely above 3-4°F). University notes on global temperature patterns: equatorial stations such as Pontianak vary by 2°C or less between months. Note only: the hottest areas shift with the season (North Africa and south-west Asia in July; Australia, southern Africa and South America in January). The claim is limited to 'naby die ewenaar', where it holds.

items.bewering: Buite die warm band is Januarie die warm tyd in die suidelike halfrond. In die noordelike halfrond is dit dan die koue tyd. In Julie is dit andersom.
items.bron: NOAA National Data Buoy Center, 'Seasons' (ndbc.noaa.gov/education/seasons.shtml): 'the Northern Hemisphere is experiencing Winter while the Southern Hemisphere experiences Summer'. Met Office, 'Why do we have seasons?' (2025): seasons follow the axial tilt. timeanddate.com: Southern Hemisphere meteorological summer runs 1 December to 28/29 February. 'Die warm tyd' means the warm season, which stays correct where the very warmest month is February (as at Cape Town).

items.bewering: Die gematigde en koue streke lyk op die twee kaarte baie anders.
items.bron: Ritter 'Air Temperature' and university notes: the annual range grows with latitude and is largest over continental interiors at high latitudes (Siberia, Canada). Antarctica runs from about -20 to 0°C in summer to -20 to -65°C in winter (EBSCO/savemyexams figures). Note only: the contrast is weakest over the Southern Hemisphere's temperate oceans, where water evens out the temperature. Strongly true over land and in the north.

items.bewering: Die kaarte wys nie een dag se temperatuur nie. Tel baie Januarie-maande se temperature op een plek saam en deel dit deur hoeveel daar is. Daardie gemiddeld staan op die kaart en sê wat daar gewoonlik gebeur.
items.bron: NOAA NCEI climate normals: a station's January normal is the average of 30 January values, each itself an average of daily observations, computed to WMO rules (current period 1991-2020). Canadian National Atlas: the January/July maps show mean daily temperature. Simplified, but the method stated (add many Januaries and divide by their number) is correct.

items.bewering: Die Januarie- en Julie-kaarte praat daarom oor die klimaat en nie oor die weer nie.
items.bron: NOAA Ocean Service, 'What's the difference between weather and climate?' (oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/weather_climate.html): 'Weather reflects short-term conditions of the atmosphere'; 'climate is the average daily weather for an extended period of time at a certain location'.

items.bewering: temperatuurkaart: 'n Kaart wat met kleure wys hoe warm dit op plekke is.
items.bron: Read as if the rest of the lesson were deleted. True of the common coloured temperature map (Australian Space Agency; Colorado State Climate Center, as above). Note only: maps that use isotherm lines without colour fills are also temperature maps (Merriam-Webster 'isotherm'). The definition describes the usual form and does not claim it is the only one. Not false.

items.bewering: gematigde streek: Een van die twee streke tussen die warm streek om die ewenaar en die koue streke by die pole.
items.bron: Read alone. AMS Glossary 'temperate belt' and Wikipedia 'Geographical zone': there are two temperate zones, North and South, each lying between the hot/torrid belt and a cold cap/frigid zone around a pole. Consistent with the study text: one warm region, two temperate regions, two cold regions.

items.bewering: gemiddelde temperatuur: Die getal wat jy kry as jy baie gemete temperature saamtel en deur hulle aantal deel.
items.bron: Read alone. This is the arithmetic mean, which is how NOAA NCEI builds monthly and 30-year normals (averages of observed values). Correct.

opsomming: All 23 claims check out against web sources, the lesson has no analogies and its two 'grootste deel' superlatives are correctly qualified, and the three regions hold together as a set for where they lie and how warm they are through the year; five optional precision notes are recorded but none is an error (a temperatuurkaart can also use isotherm lines; about nine-tenths of Brazil is tropical, not only the north; the equator is an imaginary line; block 4's general opening is qualified by its neighbours; the January/July contrast is weak over the southern oceans).
